events.text: {bk4_beasts} know you now. A cloud-crane lands on your railing as if by appointment and regards you with one gold eye. It does not call. It waits. Behind it, on the next ledge, a second creature sits, and a third beyond that: all of them turned toward you, all of them silent, all of them aware of something in you that has your {bk4_kin} in it, old and unmistakable.

choices.text: Answer them, in the old way

effects.log: You answer with a sound you did not know you could make. The crane inclines its head, and the ledge relaxes.

choices.text: Hold still, and let them look

effects.log: You hold still. After a while, one by one, they leave. The blood does not.

events.text: At dusk the weather-beasts of the Isles gather near your seat. It is not a threat. They sit on every cornice, tucked wing to wing, and the cloud around you hums softly with the blood of {bk4_kin}, as if the whole sky had remembered a name. Your servants shut the shutters. You, for your part, find you are standing at the window.

choices.text: Go out onto the balcony and call back

effects.log: The call surprises you. They answer, a hundred throats at once, and the sky is full for a moment.

choices.text: Close the shutters and wait for dawn

effects.log: You close them. In the morning the balcony is covered in feathers.

events.text: Cloud-beasts follow you through the market of the Floating Isles, at a respectful distance, like a very quiet procession. A tea-seller crosses her arms and says it has been going on all week. They know your blood, she says: {bk4_kin}, plain as a signature. You can answer them or you can ignore them, but you can no longer pretend they are not there.

choices.text: Turn and greet them

effects.log: You greet them. A small gray beast steps forward, and puts its head in your hand.

choices.text: Walk on and say nothing

effects.log: You walk on. They follow for an hour and then, one by one, peel away.

events.text: A registrar of the Jade Court's bloods arrives with a ledger the length of a cloud-barge. Your name is entered in it, in a column you did not know existed. {bk4_kin} is a bloodline of record, he says, and the Court likes to keep such things tidy. He is perfectly civil. He would like you to sign, or he would like to hear why not.

choices.text: Hide what you can, and sign only the minimum

effects.log: You sign a thin version of the truth. The registrar reads it twice, and writes something small in the margin.

choices.text: Face him, and enter the whole record

effects.log: You enter it all. He looks up, mildly surprised, and shakes your hand.

events.text: The registrar of bloods does not come in person. A summons does, with a seal and a list of questions about the creatures that visit your terrace. {bk4_kin} is mentioned by name in the third line. The answers are due by the next full moon. A neighbour has told you what happened to the last household that answered fully, and what happened to the last that did not.

choices.text: Answer in half-truths, and bury the rest

effects.log: You write a careful, dull report. It is accepted, and the matter sleeps.

choices.text: Appear in person, and tell it plainly

effects.log: You tell it plainly. The registrar listens, and writes nothing at all.

events.text: Two clerks of the Court of Bloods come to check your terrace, with measuring cords and an apologetic air. They find {bk4_kin} in the feathers, in the stains, in the ring of scratches on the railing. They do not accuse you. They only point, and ask what each thing is, and wait. The younger one, you notice, is trying very hard not to look at the sky.

choices.text: Explain nothing, and offer them tea

effects.log: They drink it with great seriousness. The record is amended to read: inconclusive.

choices.text: Show them the whole terrace, proudly

effects.log: You do. The younger clerk, to everyone's surprise, asks if she may sketch.

events.text: An old keeper of the Isles' blood finds you at a feeding-ledge, a stooped person in a coat of mended cloud-silk. They have kept {bk4_beasts} for longer than anyone remembers, and they say so without boasting. They look at you for a long moment, and say that the old blood has been looking for you, and that it is a relief to see it has been found.

choices.text: Ask what the old blood wants of you

effects.log: The keeper tells you, slowly. It is less than you feared, and more than you can promise.

choices.text: Ask the keeper to teach you the feeding-calls

effects.log: They teach you three. You practise them until the cranes come.

events.text: The keeper has a nest of small cloud-things in a basket by the door, and does not explain. They show you the oldest scrolls of the Isles' blood, written on bark, and read you one line from each. The line about {bk4_kin} is brief and not unkind. It says the blood is not a debt, only a door. It does not say which way the door opens.

choices.text: Ask the keeper to read it again

effects.log: They read it again. The second time the meaning is different, and you do not ask for a third.

choices.text: Take one of the nest-things home

effects.log: It sleeps in your sleeve. It has opinions about breakfast.

events.text: At the edge of the Isles a keeper of the old blood sits mending a net that holds nothing. They do not look up when you approach. They say, to the net, that your blood is one of the last of its line in these clouds, and that someone should have told you sooner. The keeper's voice has the small dry crack of a person who has been alone with animals too long.

choices.text: Sit with them, and mend a knot

effects.log: You mend a knot. They say nothing, and the quiet is the best thing you have been offered in a year.

choices.text: Ask what the line owes the Isles

effects.log: The keeper laughs, short and kind. "Nothing," they say. "That is what makes it hard."

events.text: {bk4_beasts} know your blood. The tigers of the high passes gather at the edge of your domain at dusk, tawny shapes in the grass, and watch your temple with a stillness that has weight. Among the offerings left at the Gate Shrine this morning is a single striped feather, though tigers have none. It is a gesture, and it is {bk4_kin} that it is addressed to.

choices.text: Answer them, from the shrine steps

effects.log: You answer with a low, rolling call. The grass answers back, and the tigers settle.

choices.text: Hold still, and let the watching pass

effects.log: You hold still. The tigers leave at dawn. The feather stays.

events.text: A procession of beasts comes to your domain's border, uninvited: hares, deer, a heron, and far behind them, a great tawny cat. Horang's domain is their country, and your blood is the old blood of it. They bow, each in its own way. The priests of your temple have shut the doors. You find yourself at the open gate, with {bk4_kin} stirring in your wrists.

choices.text: Step out and receive them

effects.log: You step out. They part around you like water, and the great cat lowers its head.

choices.text: Stay behind the gate and let them pass

effects.log: They pass, some slowly. The gate holds, and so do you.

events.text: In the Hall of Prayers an altar-cat that has never spoken to anyone looks at you and yawns. It is not an insult. It is recognition, of the kind that has no words. {bk4_beasts} have begun to leave small things on your steps: a stone, a pine-cone, a tooth. {bk4_kin} runs in you clear as a brook, and the beasts, it seems, have been waiting a long time to say so.

choices.text: Pick up the tooth, and keep it

effects.log: It is warm. You carry it, and the beasts take note of the carrying.

choices.text: Sweep the steps clean each morning

effects.log: You sweep. The offerings return, small and stubborn.

events.text: A charge of mixed blood is lodged before the Heavenly Court. The charge names {bk4_kin} in your veins, and the Court takes a keen interest in such matters, mostly because it has a form for them. An advocate arrives with a calm face and a long scroll, and offers to read it to you. You listen to the first clause, and are asked to choose your reply.

choices.text: Hide the blood, and plead pure descent

effects.log: You plead it. The advocate writes, and does not look up, and the Court is not entirely satisfied.

choices.text: Face the charge, and own the blood

effects.log: You own it. The advocate sets down the pen. The Court hears you out with unusual care.

events.text: The Heavenly Court has found a fault in your lineage. Two advocates call at your temple, in matching robes, with a charge of mixed blood and an offer to forget it for a small admission. {bk4_kin} is the name on the page. They are courteous. They are patient. They are, by profession, entirely uninterested in whether you are guilty, only in which door you will walk through.

choices.text: Admit nothing, and let them wait

effects.log: You say nothing at all. They finish their tea, and the charge remains pending.

choices.text: Admit it all, and let the Court decide

effects.log: You admit it. They exchange a glance, and write at length.

events.text: A clerk of the Court of Blood comes to your Gate Shrine with a cold voice and a warm cloak, and presents a charge. Mixed blood, it says, is no crime in itself; it is a question of record. {bk4_kin} is the mixture. The clerk has been told to extract a statement, willing or not. The clerk would prefer willing. The Court, after all, has an appetite for tidy files.

choices.text: Give a statement that says very little

effects.log: The statement is correct, polite, and empty. The clerk reads it, and nods, with respect.

choices.text: Give a statement that says everything

effects.log: It takes an hour. The clerk is silent at the end, and then asks for tea.

events.text: A keeper of the old blood of Horang's domain sits by a spring in the high pass and does not rise when you arrive. They are old, spare and patient as a boulder. Beasts sleep around them in a loose ring. They look at you for the length of a breath and say that {bk4_kin} has been missed, and that they are glad to see the blood walk into the light.

choices.text: Ask what the old blood is owed

effects.log: The keeper says it is owed only a visit now and then. It is the smallest bill you have ever been presented.

choices.text: Ask to be shown the spring

effects.log: They show you. The water is cold, and tastes of snow and iron and something older.

events.text: The keeper has a gift: a small carved tiger, grey with handling, no larger than a fist. It was given to them by the one who came before, they say, who had it from the one before that. {bk4_kin} is in the grain of the wood. They put it in your hand without ceremony, and look away, as one does when a thing is placed in trust.

choices.text: Take the tiger, and keep it close

effects.log: It is warm from their hand. You carry it everywhere.

choices.text: Ask the keeper to hold it a while longer

effects.log: They agree. The tiger stays in their hand, for now.

events.text: At the edge of Horang's domain a keeper of the old blood sits mending a long net of grass-rope. They do not look up. They say the net is for no purpose, only to keep the hands busy while the blood remembers. {bk4_beasts} have been going by all day, quietly, as if in a procession. The keeper adds that they have been your kin for longer than you have had a name.

choices.text: Sit and mend a loop or two

effects.log: You mend a loop. They say nothing, and the silence is a kindness.

choices.text: Ask how long the blood has waited

effects.log: They tell you. It is a very long time. They do not say it sorrowfully.

events.text: {bk4_beasts} know your blood. A fox sits at the edge of your fields at dawn, a lean red shape in the frost, and watches the house. It does not run. By the well a pair of crows have been waiting since before the rooster. {bk4_kin} runs in you, quite plainly, and every creature within a mile has heard of it. The dog at your door whines and then is quiet.

choices.text: Go out and meet the fox

effects.log: You go. It lets you come near, and sniffs the air, and decides.

choices.text: Stay indoors till the fox is gone

effects.log: You stay in. The fox leaves at noon. The crows leave a feather.

events.text: On market day the animals behave oddly. The horses refuse to be tied near you. A flock of sparrows rises when you pass and settles again behind. A goat butts the stall to follow you. {bk4_beasts} know the old blood of {bk4_kin} in you as a dog knows its master's step, and they cannot keep from showing it. The stallholders watch with narrowed eyes.

choices.text: Greet the goat, and let it follow

effects.log: The goat follows to the edge of town. It is not a bad companion.

choices.text: Walk fast and keep your head down

effects.log: You do. By the gate the sparrows have lost interest.

events.text: Wild things come near your house in the long evenings. A hedgehog under the porch. A heron on the roof. A line of ants across the kitchen floor that stops precisely at your boots. {bk4_kin} has made you a sort of landmark for {bk4_beasts}, and they come to look. Your neighbours have started to knock before entering, and to keep their children close.

choices.text: Leave out a bowl of water for them

effects.log: The bowl is empty by morning. A feather sits in it.

choices.text: Close the shutters at dusk and keep quiet

effects.log: The shutters hold. The sounds outside are patient and long.

events.text: A hunter of the old kind arrives in your valley, a grim, tidy person with a pelt-trimmed cloak and a rope of teeth around the neck. Beast-blood is their trade, and they say so over a mug of cider. They have heard of {bk4_kin} in these parts. They do not accuse. They only say it is an interesting thing to hear of, and ask what you might know about it.

choices.text: Hide it, and give an honest-sounding blank

effects.log: You give it. The hunter nods slowly, drinks, and keeps looking.

choices.text: Face the hunter, and tell the truth

effects.log: You tell it. The hunter sets down the mug and says they have not heard anyone say it so plainly.

events.text: A woman of the trapping guild calls at your gate with a pair of apprentices and a questionnaire. The valley's beasts, she says, have been acting strangely, and strange beasts mean strange blood. {bk4_kin} is the name that comes up. She is polite. The apprentices are not. They stand with their hands on their belts, looking at your roof, your well, the dog.

choices.text: Deny all knowledge, and serve tea

effects.log: You serve it. She drinks it, and the questionnaire is left half done.

choices.text: Invite them in, and answer every question

effects.log: You answer all of them. By the end she has stopped writing.

events.text: At the inn a hunter you have never met sits down across from you and says, softly, that they have followed a trail of paw-prints and feathers right to your table. {bk4_kin} is in your blood, they say, and they say it without hostility, as a doctor names a condition. Whatever you answer, they add, will be remembered. The innkeeper has found something to polish at the far end of the room.

choices.text: Laugh it off and change the subject

effects.log: You do, with some effort. The hunter smiles and lets the subject rest.

choices.text: Put your hands flat on the table and admit it

effects.log: You admit it. The hunter exhales, and the room lets go of a held breath.

events.text: An old woman at the edge of the forest, who keeps goats and bees and does not hold with towns, stops you on the path. She has known {bk4_kin} in her time, she says, in a face much like yours. The blood runs in families here, though few remember. She offers you a clay cup of honey-water, and says that the beasts have been telling her about you for a year.

choices.text: Drink the honey-water, and ask what they said

effects.log: It is sweet and cold. What the beasts said is brief, and you keep it.

choices.text: Ask her to teach you the old calls

effects.log: She teaches you three. They are plainer than you expected, and more powerful.

events.text: In a barn at the end of a long lane a keeper of old things shows you a row of wooden masks, each carved with a beast's face. The oldest is a fox. {bk4_kin} is there, in the grain, in the eyes. The keeper says nothing of its meaning. They only hold it up to the light and let you look, and the light is kind to it.

choices.text: Ask to hold the fox mask

effects.log: It is lighter than you thought. It fits your face, almost.

choices.text: Thank the keeper, and leave the masks as they are

effects.log: You leave them. The keeper nods, and hangs the fox back on its nail.

events.text: A keeper of the old blood lives in a hut where three paths meet, and does not welcome visitors. They let you in because of {bk4_kin}, they say, and for no other reason. There is a fire, a pot, a cat. They tell you a long story about {bk4_beasts} and the people who kept them, and the ending is not tidy. It is, however, true.

choices.text: Listen to the end, and say nothing

effects.log: You listen. The fire burns low. The cat falls asleep on your boot.

choices.text: Ask what happened to the people in the story

effects.log: The keeper looks at the fire. "They became us," they say.

events.text: A sky-whale passes the edge of your isle at midnight, so large its shadow drains the lamps. It slows. A single huge eye rolls toward you, and {bk4_kin} stirs in you like a bell answering a bell. The whale does not sing. It hangs there, a hill of patient flesh, and lets the old blood do the greeting. Your hands are shaking.

choices.text: Hum back the note the blood gives you

effects.log: The whale's eye closes in something like contentment. It drifts away trailing a low, grateful sound.

choices.text: Draw the curtains and wait for it to pass

effects.log: The shadow passes. In the morning there are ripples in the garden pond that no wind made.

events.text: The cloud-swallows of your isle have started nesting on your windowsill. Not near it, on it, in a neat row, as if the sill were a shelf. {bk4_beasts} recognise the old blood in you and have drafted you into some ancient arrangement. A swallow drops a feather in your teacup, with the air of delivering a notice.

choices.text: Leave the window open, and put out seed

effects.log: The swallows take the seed, and the window, and by spring you share the room.

choices.text: Shut the window, and let them find another ledge

effects.log: They find several. The feather stays in the cup.

events.text: A child at the market of the Floating Isles points at you and says, loudly, that you smell like a nest. The adults hush her, but they are looking. Behind the stalls, the cloud-ponies are whinnying, one after another, in a wave that reaches you. {bk4_kin} is, apparently, no secret to anyone with a tail.

choices.text: Crouch and let the child smell your sleeve

effects.log: She does, solemnly, and pronounces it a very good nest. The adults laugh in relief.

choices.text: Pull your hood forward and move on

effects.log: The ponies follow your progress down the lane with their ears.

events.text: At the foot of the White Stairs sits a very old cloud-fox, grey about the muzzle, and it bows as you approach. Stair-sweepers freeze with brooms in mid-air. The fox has not bowed to any person in living memory. {bk4_kin} runs in you, plain and unsought, and the fox, having paid its respects, merely waits for you to return them.

choices.text: Bow back, as low as the fox did

effects.log: The fox yips once, delighted, and trots away. Sweepers resume sweeping, whispering.

choices.text: Nod, and take the stairs without breaking stride

effects.log: The fox watches you climb. It is still sitting there at dusk.

events.text: A storm of cloud-moths descends on your balcony at dusk, soft and silver, and settles on the rail, the plants, your shoulders. They do not flutter or feed. They are merely counted, as if by a census. {bk4_kin} is ancient enough that all {bk4_beasts} seem to have a line in the roll for you, and the moths, apparently, have come to collect it.

choices.text: Stand still and let them settle

effects.log: They settle. Each leaves a tiny weight, and when they rise, you feel oddly recorded.

choices.text: Sweep them off the balcony gently

effects.log: They flow away like smoke, and return, the following night, in the same order.

events.text: A crane-rider falls from the sky into your courtyard, her mount unhurt, and you are the first to reach her. The crane stares at you throughout, without blinking. When the rider wakes she says only that her crane has never allowed a stranger so close. {bk4_kin} has made you something other than a stranger to {bk4_beasts}, whatever you choose.

choices.text: Tend the rider, and speak softly to the crane

effects.log: The crane lowers its neck. When the rider leaves it brushes your hair with its beak.

choices.text: Send for a healer and stay out of the crane's way

effects.log: The healer comes. The crane never takes its eyes off you.

events.text: You wake to find your bed ringed with sleeping creatures: a cloud-hare, two ferrets of the high ledges, a kit of something with too many tails. They have come in through the shutter in the night and curled up around you, ribs rising and falling together. {bk4_kin} is in you like a lullaby, and the room is warm with it.

choices.text: Lie still until they wake on their own

effects.log: They wake one by one, stretch, and leave, polite as lodgers.

choices.text: Rise and open the shutters wide

effects.log: They scatter into the light. The bed keeps their shape for a day.

events.text: A registrar's runner delivers a stamped notice: the Court of Bloods will conduct a visit to your isle regarding {bk4_kin}. No date is given. Your servants begin to dust everything in sight. Three days later a young assistant arrives with no ledger and no seal, only a paper fan, and asks, mildly, whether he might sit in your garden a while.

choices.text: Show him only the garden and nothing more

effects.log: He sits, sips, and looks. At day's end he thanks you and writes a short line that you cannot read.

choices.text: Take him round the whole isle, and answer what he asks

effects.log: He asks little. He writes less. In the end he shakes your hand twice.

events.text: A hunter of the Court of Bloods has put a lure on your terrace: a bowl of milk, a dish of fish, a carved perch. All are carefully placed to see what visits {bk4_kin}'s household. A cloud-cat sits beside the bowl, utterly composed, and when you come out, it licks a paw and pretends it has been there for hours.

choices.text: Remove the lures and say nothing of them

effects.log: The terrace is bare again by noon. The cat looks betrayed.

choices.text: Leave them where they are, and invite the hunter to tea

effects.log: The hunter comes, sheepish. The cat hops onto the table first.

events.text: The Court of Bloods issues a public bulletin: certain households of the Isles are to be examined for beast-kin descent. Yours is not named, but the list ends in "and others". Your neighbour across the gulf shuts her shutters. A sealed envelope arrives at your door with a questionnaire in the tidy script of a clerk who truly enjoys forms.

choices.text: Answer in careful half-truths

effects.log: The questionnaire is returned stamped and approved. Something in the clerk's signature looks sceptical.

choices.text: Answer every question honestly, in full

effects.log: The clerk writes to say your answers are the most complete in decades. A small gift of tea arrives.

events.text: A pair of auditors from the Jade Court lean over the rail of your isle's landing with a measuring-cord. They are counting nests. {bk4_kin} is a bloodline of interest, they say, and the number of {bk4_beasts} on your land is a figure the Court would like to understand. One of them has a cold. Both are determined.

choices.text: Hide the nests under a rented canopy

effects.log: The auditors measure the canopy instead. They seem content, and slightly bored.

choices.text: Walk them round the nests and name every inhabitant

effects.log: You name forty-one. The cold-sufferer sniffs and says he will remember them.

events.text: A rival of your house informs the Court of Bloods about the visitors to your terrace, and an inspector arrives with a small bronze bell. It is said to ring only near beast-kin. It is silent in your hallway, silent in the garden, and then, as you pass the nursery of the cloud-pup you have been raising, it rings once, sharply.

choices.text: Pocket the bell with a smile, and claim it is faulty

effects.log: The inspector frowns, but does not take it back. It rings quietly in your drawer.

choices.text: Hold the bell out and let it ring in the open

effects.log: The inspector listens to it, and to you. He leaves the bell as a gift.

events.text: At the harbour of the Floating Isles a hunter of the Court of Bloods sets up a table with a lantern and a stack of forms. Anyone with beast-kin descent, the sign says, may declare themselves for a modest tax relief. A long line forms. You stand in it, since to stand out of it is also noticed. The line shuffles forward one dull inch at a time.

choices.text: Declare yourself at the table, under a partial name

effects.log: The clerk writes a version of you. You will meet it again in future paperwork.

choices.text: Declare yourself in full, and take the relief

effects.log: The line behind you hushes, then clears its throat. Several of them also step forward.

events.text: An envoy of the Court of Bloods arrives in a barge hung with silk, and does not disembark. Instead a plank is lowered, and a very junior secretary walks across with a scroll. It lists, in neat columns, every unusual animal seen on your isle in the last year, with dates. The secretary looks at you apologetically, as if embarrassed by their employers.

choices.text: Dispute the dates, and plant doubt in the columns

effects.log: The secretary takes notes, murmurs, and quietly corrects one entry in your favour.

choices.text: Confirm the columns and add three entries they missed

effects.log: The secretary stares. The envoy, on the barge, is heard to laugh.

events.text: A keeper of the Isles' blood sits at the end of a long pier, tying knots into a rope of braided feathers. They offer you the other end. {bk4_kin} has been missed in the keeping-rolls for a long time, they say, and the rope is how they tell who has come home. It already has many knots.

choices.text: Tie a knot of your own into the rope

effects.log: The knot pulls tight. The rope hums, faintly, as if remembering.

choices.text: Ask what each knot stands for

effects.log: They name them, one by one. Some are names. Some are weather.

events.text: A keeper of the old blood has a small school for cloud-fledglings in a hollow of the Isles. They invite you to watch a morning lesson. The fledglings cluster in a row, clumsy as new coin. {bk4_beasts} learn the art of falling before the art of flight, the keeper says, and you recognise something of yourself in the fumbling.

choices.text: Stay for the lesson, and help catch the fallers

effects.log: You catch four. Each one regards you as a sort of cloud.

choices.text: Ask the keeper how they learned to teach

effects.log: They shrug, and say by being taught poorly, once, and remembering.

events.text: In a cave under the largest isle, a keeper of the old blood has gathered the shed feathers of three hundred years. They are sorted by colour and season, in wooden drawers. They pull one out, grey-green and tipped with gold, and lay it on your palm. {bk4_kin}, they say, flew once with such a plume, and it was the finest in the sky.

choices.text: Ask to keep the feather

effects.log: The keeper lets you, after thought. It weighs nothing, and it is the first thing you reach for in a hurry.

choices.text: Ask who wore it, and how it ended

effects.log: The keeper tells you. It ends gently, which you had not expected.

events.text: A keeper of the old blood hands you a cup of water from the spring beneath the Isles, saying only that it was drunk by your line. {bk4_beasts} gather in the cave mouth to watch you drink the water, as at a wedding. The water is cold and tastes of stone and, faintly, of a childhood you cannot remember. The keeper looks at the floor to give you privacy.

choices.text: Drink all of the water

effects.log: You do. The beasts give a low collective sigh, and the keeper wipes their eyes.

choices.text: Pour half back on the stone

effects.log: You pour. The stone drinks it. The keeper nods, as at the right answer.

events.text: At dusk a keeper of the old blood teaches you the Isles' lullaby, the one all {bk4_beasts} know in their sleep. It has no words, only a long falling line. The keeper hums it first, then waits. You hum it back. A cloud-lamb in a basket by the fire sighs and goes completely limp. The keeper says: that is how you know.

choices.text: Hum it again, softer

effects.log: The lamb sleeps. The keeper smiles at the fire, pleased and a little wistful.

choices.text: Ask where the song came from

effects.log: The keeper does not know. They say that is the song's way: to be remembered more than explained.

events.text: A keeper of the old blood keeps a ledger of {bk4_kin}'s descendants and finds, tonight, that it is one name short. Yours was left out, by a clerk's slip two centuries ago. They offer to add it now, in their own hand, if you will sit while they do. The ink is made from walnut and soot. It smells like a library in autumn.

choices.text: Sit, and let them write it

effects.log: The name goes in, cleanly. The keeper blots it and closes the book with a pat.

choices.text: Ask to write it yourself

effects.log: You do, in a shaky hand. The keeper says that is the correct way.

events.text: A keeper of the old blood is training a cloud-heron to carry messages between isles, and the heron has chosen to practise on you. For a week it brings you small notes written in the keeper's cramped hand: weather, news, and once a recipe. Eventually you pay a visit, and the heron lands on your shoulder, smug, and the keeper says: well, now you've been delivered.

choices.text: Write back, and send it by the heron

effects.log: The heron takes it, hesitates, and goes. The reply comes before noon.

choices.text: Ask the keeper to teach you the heron's ways

effects.log: They teach you three small courtesies. The heron approves of one.

events.text: The snakes of the lower garden gather in a ring beneath your window at the hour of the lamp. They are the small, harmless kind, and they twist into letters that spell, with some effort, a single word: kin. {bk4_kin} runs in you, deep and unmistakable, and {bk4_beasts} are saying hello the only way snakes can.

choices.text: Lean from the window and hiss softly back

effects.log: The letters scramble in delight. The ring dissolves into a happy tangle.

choices.text: Close the window and leave them be

effects.log: They hold the letters until dawn, then slither off. The shape lingers in the dust.

events.text: During a festival of Haeryong's waters, the carp in the temple pond all turn to face your seat at once, mouths opening and closing in time. Worshippers stop their chant. {bk4_kin} has been recognised, loudly and in public, by a hundred fish, and the pond-keeper is looking at you as if you owed him an explanation.

choices.text: Kneel at the pond and answer the carp

effects.log: You call to them in the old tongue. The pond ripples, and the keeper lowers his head.

choices.text: Remain in your seat, and let the chant resume

effects.log: The chant resumes. The carp face you through the entire hymn.

events.text: A flock of temple doves lands on your shoulders when you step into the sunlit court, five or six of them, grumbling softly. They have never done this before. {bk4_beasts} have been feeling for the old blood in you, they seem to say, and you have been standing in the sun for it. The sacristan drops his broom.

choices.text: Hold out a hand and let them perch

effects.log: They arrange themselves along your arm like ornaments, and the sacristan weeps.

choices.text: Stand very still until they lose interest

effects.log: They lose interest after a quarter hour. A single feather drifts down.

events.text: At the turning of the year the hounds of the Court of Hunt gather at your gate, tongues lolling, utterly docile. They are normally savage with strangers. {bk4_kin} lies in you like a banked fire, and the hounds know it. Their master, a lean god in a leather coat, stands behind them with a surprised look and a coil of rope.

choices.text: Walk among the hounds, and scratch their ears

effects.log: They fall in around you, wagging. The master rolls up his rope in awe.

choices.text: Wait at the gate until the master calls them off

effects.log: He calls. They go, reluctantly, looking back.

events.text: A tortoise the size of a small hill wanders into your temple precinct from the lower marshes and settles in the central court. It does not move for three days. Priests bring it lettuce. Pilgrims touch its shell for luck. On the fourth day it looks up at you, slow and ancient, and {bk4_kin} stirs in your bones like a tide.

choices.text: Sit beside it, and keep it company

effects.log: You sit. It says nothing for hours. When it moves on, you feel somehow accompanied.

choices.text: Order the priests to feed it, and leave it alone

effects.log: The tortoise accepts the lettuce with dignity. It leaves at the first frost.

events.text: A bear walks out of the forest at the edge of the domain, stands upright at the shrine gate, and bows. Several junior priests faint. The bear then sits, as a bear does, and waits. {bk4_beasts} send their elders to recognise {bk4_kin} in a god's veins, and this one has come on foot, with honey on his paws.

choices.text: Bow back and accept the honey

effects.log: It is thick and wild. The bear eats the rest and sleeps on your steps.

choices.text: Send an acolyte to ask what he wants

effects.log: The acolyte returns pale and confused. The bear stays a week.

events.text: In the night a pack of wolves draws up below the walls of your temple, grey shapes on the snow, and sings. It is not a hunting song. It is the long quavering one the old tales call the greeting of blood. {bk4_kin} answers in your chest before you can stop it. Your priests huddle in the colonnade with their lamps shaking.

choices.text: Climb the wall and howl back

effects.log: The pack falls silent, then answers, rich and rolling. It is an astonishing sound.

choices.text: Keep the lamps low and the doors barred

effects.log: They sing till dawn and leave. The snow is covered in tracks that all lead toward you.

events.text: A clerk of the Court of Blood, thin and exact, sets up a desk in your temple porch and lays out a stack of forms headed "Declaration of Descent". {bk4_kin} is a bloodline of record, he says, and the Heavenly Court requires an updated entry. He has brought his own ink. He does not look up.

choices.text: Fill the form cunningly, leaving out the best parts

effects.log: The clerk reads it, sighs, and files it with a faint air of disappointment.

choices.text: Fill it in truthfully and sign with a flourish

effects.log: The clerk reads it twice and looks up, surprised and almost shy.

events.text: A rival god lodges a petition with the Court of Blood alleging that your temple harbours unregistered beast-kin, namely you, and requests inspection. The inspector arrives on a donkey, which is how you can tell the Court is serious. {bk4_beasts} have been seen to bow to you, and this is entered as evidence.

choices.text: Receive the inspector, and say the bowing was courtesy

effects.log: The inspector makes a face, and writes courtesy. The donkey eats your hedge.

choices.text: Receive the inspector, and say what you are

effects.log: The inspector leans back on the cushion. "Well," he says, and writes for a long time.

events.text: A shrine-hunter of the divine registry has been following the trail of {bk4_beasts} across three domains, and it ends at your temple door. She stands there with a notebook and an apple. She has tracked more beast-kin than anyone alive, she says, and has never once been wrong. She asks if she may sit in your garden and watch, only watch.

choices.text: Say she may watch, and keep your garden plain

effects.log: She sits for three days, and sees little. She leaves puzzled, and without the apple.

choices.text: Say she may watch, and let your garden be itself

effects.log: The garden fills with creatures. She weeps into the notebook and eats her apple.

events.text: A summons is read aloud in your temple by a herald in blue: the Court of Blood commands the attendance of the god {bk4_kin}'s line is traced to, at the next full moon. Your high priest stares at his own shoes. The herald rolls up the scroll and looks at the sun, as if he would rather not be here either. You are the one named.

choices.text: Attend, but give nothing away

effects.log: The Court finds your answers blank and well-prepared. The moon wanes before the matter ripens.

choices.text: Attend and recount the whole line

effects.log: The Court hears it out. It is a long, and surprisingly moving, afternoon.

events.text: A quiet agent of the divine registry joins your temple as a lay brother, scrubbing floors with unusual care. {bk4_kin} is the agent's interest, and the agent is not good at hiding it, since they hum when scrubbing, and always hum the tunes of {bk4_beasts}. The priests like them enormously. You are the only one who knows.

choices.text: Say nothing, and let the agent scrub

effects.log: The agent stays a year. The floors have never been cleaner, and you give away very little.

choices.text: Take the agent aside and tell them everything

effects.log: The agent stops scrubbing and listens. They leave the next morning, with a very long report.

events.text: The Court of Blood holds an open day at the Gate of Registry. For a small fee any god may submit their lineage for study. Your neighbours have queued around the block. A stall sells sweet bean cakes. A clerk with a megaphone calls names. Yours is on the list, and the clerk reads it slowly, with relish.

choices.text: Slip away through the crowd before you are reached

effects.log: You are home before your name is called again, with a sweet bean cake as consolation.

choices.text: Step up to the desk and give your descent

effects.log: The clerk lowers the megaphone. The queue behind you goes quiet, then claps, unevenly.

events.text: A herald of the Court of Blood leaves a set of tiny pawprints in plaster on your doorstep, and a note: these were found in your garden. Please explain. The pawprints are exactly the size of a cat's, and also of nothing a cat has ever been. {bk4_kin} could be the explanation, but the Court would like it written down.

choices.text: Write an explanation that explains nothing

effects.log: The note is returned with a stamp reading RECEIVED. Nothing further happens.

choices.text: Write the explanation, with a sketch of the creature

effects.log: The Court sends a letter of thanks. They would like to visit the creature.

events.text: A keeper of the old blood sits in the cloister of your temple, doing nothing in particular, and when you pass they say, to the air, that {bk4_kin} is a fine thing to be. It is the first sentence they have spoken in years, according to the priests. Their eyes are the colour of old amber. The cloister has gone very still.

choices.text: Sit beside them and wait for the second sentence

effects.log: It comes at dusk. It is "thank you", and they mean it.

choices.text: Ask what they have been keeping all these years

effects.log: They show you a small clay whistle. It plays one note, which you recognise.

events.text: A keeper of the old blood has an enclosure of tiny, glowing creatures in the root-cellar of a forgotten shrine. They tend them with a spoon and a wooden bowl. {bk4_beasts} hatched from old magic, they say, and the strain was nearly lost. The creatures are the size of beans and shine faintly gold. One climbs your thumb.

choices.text: Offer to feed them next time

effects.log: The keeper looks startled and then pleased. They give you a spoon.

choices.text: Ask how many are left of the strain

effects.log: Eleven. The keeper counts them every night, and has for a century.

events.text: A keeper of the old blood meets you at a crossroads shrine, wearing a coat of badger-fur and carrying nothing. They lead you to a small stone tablet half-buried in moss. The writing on it is ancient. They read it aloud: a list of nine names, all of {bk4_kin}. The last has been chiselled half away. They look at you quietly.

choices.text: Ask whether the tenth name is yours

effects.log: They nod, and hand you a chisel. You cut a few strokes, and no more.

choices.text: Brush the moss from the tablet, and sit beside it

effects.log: You brush it clean. The keeper bows as at an altar.

events.text: A keeper of the old blood runs a very small inn at the foot of a mountain pass, serving beast-kin and no one else. {bk4_beasts} are the clientele. A fox sits in the corner nursing a bowl of broth. A raven reads the paper. The keeper sets a cup in front of you without asking. "House blend," they say.

choices.text: Drink, and listen to the room

effects.log: It is a warm and puzzling hour. You have never been so relaxed among so many strangers.

choices.text: Ask whether there is a room for the night

effects.log: They show you to one. The bed is warm already, as though someone had just left.

events.text: At the edge of the domain a keeper of the old blood is mending a fishing-net with a bone needle, humming a tune that {bk4_beasts} know. They look up when you approach and say the tune is for you, though they didn't know it until you walked up. They teach you the first three lines, slowly, and you find your mouth shaping them without effort.

choices.text: Learn the whole tune, line by line

effects.log: It takes the afternoon. When you sing the end, nearby creatures wake and listen.

choices.text: Hum along, and let them lead

effects.log: You hum. The keeper nods, as though the tune had been waiting for a second voice.

events.text: A keeper of the old blood brings an orphaned fawn to your temple door in a basket, and says nothing, only holds the basket out. {bk4_kin} is plain in the animal's eyes. Behind the keeper, the sacristan mimes frantic refusal. The fawn butts its head against the basket's edge and makes a small, outrageous noise.

choices.text: Take the basket, and name the fawn

effects.log: It sleeps on a mat by the altar. By spring it is following you to the rites.

choices.text: Ask the keeper to raise it on your behalf, with offerings

effects.log: They agree. Every month a note arrives about its weight and its bad habits.

events.text: A keeper of the old blood invites you to a funeral for a very old beast of {bk4_kin}'s line, a stag who died at the foot of a mountain. The mourners are mostly animals. A heron reads the eulogy, in an interpretive way. The keeper stands at the head of the grave and asks if you will say a word, as one of the blood.

choices.text: Say a word, plain and short

effects.log: You say it. The animals bow their heads, and the heron nods in approval.

choices.text: Stand silent beside the grave, and lay down an offering

effects.log: The offering is a sprig of pine. The keeper takes it, and sets it on the stag.

events.text: At the village well a stray dog sits down at your feet and will not be moved. The women stare. The dog stares up at you with an expression of patient certainty. {bk4_kin} runs in you, plain as a river, and {bk4_beasts} have begun to claim you as their own. The water in your bucket sloshes over the lip as you stand very still.

choices.text: Crouch and scratch the dog's ears

effects.log: The dog leans in. The women murmur, and one makes a sign against the evil eye, half-heartedly.

choices.text: Fill the bucket and walk away quickly

effects.log: The dog follows you to the end of the lane, then sits, watching you go.

events.text: A heron has taken up residence on the roof of your house. It stands on one leg for hours, motionless, and observes. The neighbours say it is a sign. Some say good, some say otherwise. {bk4_kin} is in you, and {bk4_beasts} know it as surely as the weather. The heron preens once, and resumes its stare.

choices.text: Climb up and sit beside it

effects.log: You sit. It allows it. For an hour the two of you watch the village together.

choices.text: Leave it be, and avoid looking up

effects.log: It stays through the winter. The village stops remarking on it after a month.

events.text: During the evening milking, every cow in the village shed turns its head to look at you as you pass the door, in unison, with a faint wet sound of chewing. The herd-girl drops her pail. {bk4_kin} runs in you, and {bk4_beasts} are not shy about it. The cows regard you with enormous, liquid, knowing eyes.

choices.text: Greet the cows by name

effects.log: You know none of their names. You make them up, and the cows approve.

choices.text: Pretend you are looking for something else, and back away

effects.log: You back out of the shed to a soft chorus of lowing.

events.text: A wild boar, grey-bristled and enormous, trots up the lane of your village in broad daylight and stops in front of your gate. Doors slam in every house. The boar sits down, grunts, and waits. {bk4_beasts} have sent an elder of their kind to recognise the blood of {bk4_kin}, and the elder is not in a hurry.

choices.text: Open the gate and step into the lane

effects.log: The boar grunts again, a long low note. It turns and leads you a little way out of town.

choices.text: Bolt the gate and wait for it to leave

effects.log: It leaves at dusk. The lane smells of earth and pine for days.

events.text: Every night this week an owl has landed on the sill of your window and hooted exactly three times. On the seventh night you find you are hooting back, half-asleep, without meaning to. {bk4_kin} runs in you, and {bk4_beasts} know a language you were never taught, and your throat has remembered it. The owl cocks its head, pleased.

choices.text: Hoot back deliberately, and listen to the owl's reply

effects.log: It is a conversation of seven short words. You remember all of them in the morning.

choices.text: Stuff a pillow in the window-crack and sleep

effects.log: The hooting continues outside the pillow. The owl gives up before dawn.

events.text: A traveller in a green coat, said to be a collector for the great houses, takes a room above the village inn and starts asking about animals that behave strangely. He pays well for stories. {bk4_kin} is the name he keeps circling, politely, over his stew. He does not use your name, but he does look across the room at you once, mildly.

choices.text: Spin him a boring story about a barn cat

effects.log: He listens to all of it. He pays you, and you are almost sure he does not believe it.

choices.text: Sit down with him and tell it plainly

effects.log: He puts down his spoon. He pays you triple, and says nothing about what he will do.

events.text: The village fair brings a hunter from the hill-country with a pack of lean dogs, which, one after another, sit politely in front of you. The hunter's whistle fails to move them. He has a long stare and a short temper, and he tries the whistle again. {bk4_kin} is in the air between you, and the dogs know it.

choices.text: Pretend not to notice the dogs, and walk on

effects.log: You manage it for twenty yards. The dogs follow. The hunter watches, arms crossed.

choices.text: Kneel and greet the dogs, and let the hunter see

effects.log: The hunter lowers his whistle, speechless. Then, slowly, he nods.

events.text: A clerk of the district archive visits your village to update the records, and asks the household a series of questions about grandparents and animals. {bk4_kin} is on his list, with a small mark beside the name. He is thorough and unhurried. Behind him a goat eats the corner of his register. He does not seem to notice.

choices.text: Answer vaguely, and offer him a bowl of soup

effects.log: He takes the soup. The questions grow less pointed with each spoonful.

choices.text: Answer in full, and offer him the family stories

effects.log: He writes until his hand cramps. He leaves with a gift of cheese.

events.text: A pair of brothers from the trapping guild lean on the rail of the village bridge and watch you as you cross, three days running. On the fourth day they fall into step beside you. {bk4_beasts} are rare in these parts, the elder says, and {bk4_kin} rarer. They ask, with no hostility, whether you have any pets. Their own dog sits patiently between them.

choices.text: Say you have only a cat, and that it is shy

effects.log: They look sceptical. The younger brother says he likes cats. The matter lapses.

choices.text: Introduce them to the animals that come to your door

effects.log: They sit on your step until dusk. They leave with soft faces and a promise to say nothing.

events.text: At the autumn market a woman with a falcon on her wrist stops at your stall and says the falcon will not take food from anyone but you. She says it lightly. She is a falconer of some repute from the next kingdom, and her lightness is carefully built. {bk4_kin} is plain to see if you know where to look, and she knows.

choices.text: Deny that the bird cares for you at all

effects.log: The falcon takes a strip of meat from your hand anyway. She smiles, thin and tired.

choices.text: Offer the falcon a morsel, and admit what you are

effects.log: She watches the bird eat. She says it has been a long road to find you.

events.text: An old shepherd at the high pasture, who has not come down to the village in years, flags you down from the ridge. He keeps a flock of mountain goats and a very old collie. He says {bk4_kin} is a thing his grandmother knew, and that the collie has been waiting for you, which he did not expect to live to see. The collie rises, creaking.

choices.text: Kneel and let the collie smell your hand

effects.log: It licks your wrist, once, with great ceremony. The shepherd nods.

choices.text: Ask the shepherd what his grandmother knew

effects.log: He tells you, between pulls of a pipe. It is mostly about goats, and then very suddenly not.

events.text: A beekeeper at the far end of a long valley, a thin woman with a veil rolled up on her hat, lets you into her yard and says nothing for a while. The bees circle you but do not sting. {bk4_beasts} are her business, she says, and {bk4_kin} her specialty. She hands you a comb of honey on a wooden plate.

choices.text: Eat the honey slowly, and ask about the hives

effects.log: She shows you three. In the third the queen turns to face you.

choices.text: Ask whether she knew others of the blood

effects.log: She did. She lists them, name by name, on her fingers, and runs out of fingers.

events.text: A ferrywoman who has plied the same river for fifty years keeps a family of otters under the bow of her boat. On the crossing, one of them swims up and rests its chin on your hand. The ferrywoman says {bk4_kin} was in her mother's family once, and she is glad to see it still walks the world. She does not charge you the fare.

choices.text: Thank her, and ask to hear about her mother's family

effects.log: She tells you across the whole river, and you miss your stop on purpose.

choices.text: Feed the otter a bit of bread and watch it dive

effects.log: It surfaces with a minnow, delighted with itself. The ferrywoman laughs.

events.text: A charcoal-burner in the woods tells you, between blowing on his fire and wiping his face, that he keeps the old stories of {bk4_kin}. His hut is full of soot-black carvings of foxes, hares and deer. Each, he says, is a name. He picks one up, the smallest, a hare with a notched ear, and says it is yours.

choices.text: Take the hare, and ask how he knew

effects.log: He shrugs. "Charcoal teaches you to wait," he says. The hare fits in your palm like a seed.

choices.text: Ask to hear the story that goes with the hare

effects.log: He tells it. It is short, strange and kind, and takes the whole fire to finish.

events.text: In the loft of a sleepy stable at the edge of the village, a stable-hand keeps a menagerie of orphaned creatures: a raven, a lamb, a pair of hedgehogs, one blind owl. {bk4_beasts} come to him as they come to no one, he says, and he thinks it is because of {bk4_kin}, whom he once had the luck to nurse. He looks at you a long moment. He is very old.

choices.text: Sit with the stable-hand, and help him feed the owl

effects.log: The owl takes the mouse from your fingers, delicately, and blinks its blind eyes.

choices.text: Ask whom he nursed, and how long ago

effects.log: He tells you. It was a long time ago, and the person was kind.

events.text: A woman who keeps the village graveyard also keeps a cat for every grave. They sleep on the headstones in the sun. She says the cats are descended from one who came with {bk4_kin} long ago, and that {bk4_beasts} have always known the graveyard as safe ground. She walks you among the stones and names each cat, and each cat's person.

choices.text: Walk with her, and listen to every name

effects.log: It takes the afternoon. You come away feeling you have met a village you did not know.

choices.text: Sit on a bench and let a cat choose you

effects.log: A grey one does. It stays until dark, and leaves a hair on your sleeve.
